contexts.text: Philosophers... speak of the spirit by terms which they themselves do not know...
All who reason from sensuous, scientific, and philosophical things...
Cannot be apprehended by the senses, knowledge, or philosophy.
Had confused truth and good by scientific and philosophical things.
Has extinguished spiritual ideas by the terms and definitions of human philosophy.
The more the Rational thinks from scientifics which originate from... philosophical things...
This is true, philosophically; but still the philosophers themselves... think differently.
At this day they not only reason from the senses, but also, by a philosophy unknown to the ancients, concerning Divine arcana.
Those who have wanted to penetrate Divine arcana... by philosophical things...
The more they consult... philosophical things...
But those who think from the affirmative can confirm themselves... by philosophical things.
If one is wise in philosophical things, he can confirm himself by this:...
As the word form savours of human philosophy...
(Origin of the philosophies of Aristotle.)
The philosophies (of the schoolmen) are means of being insane...
A little child speaks more philosophically... than he could describe in volumes.
When they had lived as men, they had been delighted with ideas... but without philosophy.
The scientifics which are now called philosophies, such as those of Aristotle, were unknown to the Ancients.

The scientifics which... are properly called philosophies, rather withdraw the mind from knowing such things, because they can also be applied to confirm falsities; and also let the mind into darkness when truths are confirmed by them; because very many of them are bare words, by which the confirmations are made, which are apprehended by few, and concerning which even these few dispute.
Many have become such from the confounding of good and truth by philosophical things...
A philosopher more celebrated and sane, who died some years ago, with whom I spoke concerning degrees...
The philosopher confirmed it, and avowed that such things had been known to him... and that the world should apply philosophical things to such uses...
By the sciences are meant philosophies, etc.
The Ancients, [who were] after the Most Ancients, acknowledged for wisdom the wisdom of reason; and these were called philosophers.
Three novitiates, of whom... the third was a philosopher.
The philosopher told like things about himself...
Therefore the ancient philosophers and scholastics believed that influx from (the organs of the senses) was derived into the soul.
How, from being a philosopher I became a theologian...
What Christian theologian has not studied philosophy in the schools before he is inaugurated...
There came some from the Christian world who... had been most celebrated philosophers...
Excepting the philosophers...

This understanding is not acquired through philosophy such as is this day in human minds; for this rather destroys all faith; but such as is philosophy in itself, which is true philosophy when it accords with the things in the Divine Word as do external things with internal, or as does nature in itself with Heaven... Such must be the philosophy of the human mind that by it is clearly seen what is spiritual and celestial; and such also exists, because it is such in itself...
Hence, as soon as they consult any philosophy, they fall into the worship of nature... and thus faith is almost unamendable, unless all their philosophy is first shaken off...
Who doubts more about spiritual and celestial things than those who study philosophy...
Man imbibes from himself, and from the operations of his mind, philosophical scientifics...
(Thus) how poor and [good for] nothing is philosophy...
Those who live there are such... as are of sound reason, and do not extend the philosophy of the mind into heavenly things.
Therefore faith is destroyed by human philosophy.
How they philosophize on this Earth. Described.
That philosophy is worthless. Explained.
That human philosophy has disclosed many Truths...
Thus philosophy can be present when it is a servant.
[Conversation] with a celebrated philosopher concerning certain things in philosophy.

As to philosophy, every part of it has hitherto done nothing else than darken minds, and thus close the way to the view of interior things... for it stops short in mere terms... Rational philosophy so confines the ideas that the mind cleaves in mere particulars... so that in the other life, a philosopher who has indulged much in such things, is stupid...
That philosophical things so confine the human mind that at last it can see nothing.
Concerning philosophy, useful and useless.
They represented a wild boar, with blood sprinkled on his back... because I have interspersed philosophical terms, or have formed ideas philosophically.
But they were instructed that my philosophies are nothing else than certain ideas pronounced in simpler terms. Example(s).
Thus it is a kind of philosophical speech, more concise than other speech... and, indeed, more clear...

But the abuse is that philosophers remain in terms... Thus an unlearned man has much more extended ideas, and sees what truth is better than a philosopher; for such a one remains in the mire, like a swine... and becomes a wild boar in the forests; for he ranges about... in Truths, which he tears to pieces and kills. SE 1605. SE 1606.
By human philosophy or intelligence are also meant fables... and also the magic of the Egyptians.
That the philosophy of men is only that of vocabularies.
Concerning the philosophy of man: how it blinds minds.
How base and worthless is the syllogistic philosophy...
Natural knowledges and human philosophy not only obscure, but also completely... extinguish the light of spiritual Truths.
Those who have been reduced into Falsity through philosophy...
That philosophical Truths convince such more strongly...
That philosophers who have taken up phantasies cannot believe...
Whatever philosophical and scientific is with men, they turn into confirmations.
When men reason from things philosophical, etc.
From the confusion of truth and good by philosophies and scientifics...
The philosophy (of Aristotle) has come forth from thought, (and not from terms to thought).
The philosophy of such things is of no use, except for the sake of delight.
Formerly they could think much better without philosophy...
Aristotle formed his philosophies in the natural order...
He had studied instrumental causes only, ... as philosophies, etc.
Some sciences completely destroy the faculty of thinking... as philosophies, when [a matter] is determined by a series of conclusions from definitions of terms...
Concerning philosophy and freedom.
(Philosophies included among the useful sciences.)
